suggestions.title: 1. My Brain Feels Damaged: your bleed lines first, mine after in plain words
suggestions.what: Your three bleed lines ("If someone is worried about a bleed, I'd probably skip DMSO, ..."), word for word, move to the start of the paragraph. My two sentences before them ("DMSO cannot identify whether the problem is a clot, a hemorrhage, low oxygen, an electrolyte crisis, or something else. edits.before: DMSO cannot identify whether the problem is a clot, a hemorrhage, low oxygen, an electrolyte crisis, or something else. The larger adjacent risk is losing a treatment window or missing a bleed because the symptoms improved enough to feel reassuring. If someone is worried about a bleed, I'd probably skip DMSO, but it depends on how severe their issue is. It's not a powerful blood thinner like heparin, unless maybe injected; it's basically a dietary blood thinner. I've never had any issues with bleeding too much from consuming DMSO, and never heard of it either, but if bleeding is already a medical issue I'd want to think about that more.
edits.after: If someone is worried about a bleed, I'd probably skip DMSO, but it depends on how severe their issue is. It's not a powerful blood thinner like heparin, unless maybe injected; it's basically a dietary blood thinner. I've never had any issues with bleeding too much from consuming DMSO, and never heard of it either, but if bleeding is already a medical issue I'd want to think about that more. They can feel better on DMSO with a clot or a bleed still there. So if any of the checks above fail, call medics right away, before the window for treating a stroke closes.

suggestions.title: 2. MDMA: what else to do once the jaw tenses, and which signs mean medics
suggestions.reading: The MDMA section read [AI Detected, 96%](https://www.pangram.com/history/08beb99e-4d7b-45b4-ac6f-32c9bfe3823a), this paragraph in its last AI High window, with your second wife's story.
suggestions.tested:
The two lists taken apart, the trial said as what decides it (a lot of plain water) and what to do (sip an electrolyte drink): [AI Detected, 87%](https://www.pangram.com/history/adc38bd4-0651-498e-90be-4f06c7540ad8), the first line Human Low, the water line AI Medium, the three sign lines AI High.

Each sign line built its own way: "A headache that gets worse and worse is how low sodium tends to show up, often with throwing up or confusion, and it's time to call medics. The same goes for muscles getting weaker and weaker, or palpitations where the heart skips beats, which can mean their potassium is low. And a seizure or collapse means the MDMA toxicity has become an emergency, so get medics there right away." [AI Generated, 100%](https://www.pangram.com/history/1ffa53a8-6c90-4b25-9ea5-9a1523a572cf).
suggestions.sense: A fresh reader on MDMA's signs: a headache, throwing up, a pounding heart and tired muscles come with MDMA anyway, so only "keeps getting worse" tells them something's wrong, and they can't tell low potassium from an ordinary MDMA heartbeat. Another read "drink less water" as "restrict water", which could push toward overheating; the trial's point is plain water by the bottle, and the guide already says to sip.
suggestions.why: Your story before it reads more human than anything I put after it. How you'd say what to watch for and when to call medics teaches me the guide's other "what to watch for" paragraphs.
suggestions.advice_note: Edit it: what to do after the jaw tenses and which signs mean medics, in your words. The trial (one normal dose, low sodium only in those drinking freely) stays linked on your words; the kidney review can move to the next paragraph's "acute kidney injury", which says the same.
